name: file.create
description: Create a new file with the given content. Errors with `already_exists` if the file is already present; use `file.write` to overwrite an existing file. Atomic by default — content lands in a temp file then renames into place.

path.description: Absolute path. Parent directory must exist (use directory.create first).

content.description: Content to write. base64-encoded if encoding=binary; decoded text otherwise.

encoding.description: Encoding used to interpret `content`. `binary` decodes from base64 to raw bytes; all others encode the text into the named encoding.

atomic.description: When true, write to a temp file and rename into place. When false, writes directly to path.

bytes_written.description: Number of bytes actually written to disk (after encoding from `content`). For `encoding: binary` this equals the decoded base64 length.

encoding.description: Echo of the encoding used to write. Confirms the agent honoured the requested encoding (no silent fallback).

x-implementations.name: create_file_w_atomic_new
x-implementations.description: Win32 `CreateFileW` to a sibling temp file with CREATE_NEW disposition + `WriteFile` + `MoveFileExW(MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH)` (no MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING — fails if target exists, surfaced as ERR already_exists). Used when `atomic: true`.

x-implementations.name: create_file_w_new
x-implementations.description: Win32 `CreateFileW` directly with CREATE_NEW disposition + `WriteFile`. Returns ERR already_exists if the file exists. Used when `atomic: false`.

windows-modern.description: CreateFileW with CREATE_NEW disposition. The atomic path writes to a temp file and renames in (the rename fails if target exists, returning ERR already_exists). Long paths via `\\?\` prefix automatic when input exceeds MAX_PATH.

windows-classic.description: CreateFileA on NT 4 / 9x; CreateFileW on NT 5+. CREATE_NEW disposition is universally supported; the `already_exists` semantic is identical across all classic versions.
